claims_for_review: One canonical JSON interpreter is shared by workflow, intent store, and state-contract regression.
The intent key includes run_generation while the effect key omits it.
Same key and payload reuse the original route/token; different payload conflicts.
Concurrent same-intent calls invoke one logical prepare.
A lost provider result is recovered by the same idempotent key, while blind retry and preallocated route values are rejected.
Checkpoint snapshots are revisioned and hash chained in memory; durable filesystem binding is not claimed.
No actual provider call, message send, endpoint mutation, or Router runtime mutation occurs.
review_questions: Are AC-10-A01 through A07 actually demonstrated rather than merely declared?
Is the per-intent concurrency lock linearizable for the tested cooperative process model?
Can a provider success followed by local result loss recover the original route/token without blind prepare?
Does checkpoint restore reject a tampered hash chain?
Did implementation remain within the exact six-file authorization and preserve P4 durable-store ownership?
Are there any blocking correctness, replay, key-identity, or scope defects before P2b can be marked complete?
